analysis:
The PR modifies only docs/architecture/inference.md; no executable code or security control changes are visible. The patch excerpt is truncated, but the head text shows large documentation additions (head ranges 617-856 and others) for the Nemotron Super managed slot, GLM5Next boundary, image/video admission, prefix-bank sizing and cache-scope behavior. The one visible changed table row (line 607) says a refused SSD store's typed reason reaches the bridge for local `/metrics` only. That is a documentation claim about information flow. I cannot verify the `/metrics` exposure or that the reason stays off the coordinator/consumer path, because no source was supplied. The reason is a typed refusal code, not prompt content, so it is unlikely to touch A-001.

Documented security-relevant claims worth confirming against code in other passes:
- Text prefix reuse is partitioned by authenticated cache scope and is off without one (lines 232-238, 522-524). This matches T-041's coordinator-authored scope. The documented prefix bank for the Super slot is a resident-RAM bank. T-041 says production has no RAM prefix tier, only the encrypted SSD tier. The doc describes an engine-internal hybrid checkpoint bank, scope-partitioned, so there may be a threat-model wording gap, but this is not proven to be a regression. It is unverified and does not qualify as a finding.
- Media admission bounds (8 MiB body, ingress and media memory reservations, video decode allowance) are documented as DoS mitigations; I could not verify the enforcement.
- The Super slot emits no cache receipts or prefix-cache capability.

No concrete regression is identified from the documentation alone. Because the cache-bank claims touch T-041 and their implementation is outside the supplied evidence, a human or code-level pass may want to confirm that the Super hybrid bank respects the cache-scope partition and TTL/at-rest assumptions. I set needs_deeper_review to false since this is documentation-only.
